about: The transit systems the transit ride types use (core.transit), each from its own static GTFS, fetched and compacted on the host (scripts/fetch_transit_gtfs.py, scripts/build_transit_schedule.py; docs/OPERATIONS.md). The feeds and the file built from them are never committed (docs/SOURCES.md). `bike.vehicle`: all = every trip takes a bike; trip = only trips with GTFS bikes_allowed 1; offpeak = every trip outside weekday rush (06:00-09:30, 15:00-19:00); none = no bike (unclear bike access is closed). `bike.station`: elevator = the map's Metro elevators (WMATA); step_free = GTFS wheelchair_boarding 1 on the stop or its station, unknown is closed; any = a bus stop at the curb. `words` names a vehicle in a step: {route} is the route's name. `idle_notes`: say plainly when a route near the trip has no service at that time.

bike.rule: Bikes are allowed on Metro at all hours: use the elevators, board by a car's end doors, at most four bikes a car. Metro may restrict bikes during special events or crowding.
Each Metrobus has a front rack for two bikes.

Full-size bikes are allowed on every MARC train, in a car marked with the green Bicycle Entrance decal or light, one bike each; bring two bungee cords. With no free bike rack, wait for the next train.
Bikes ride Light RailLink outside rush hour and special events, at most two a vehicle, in the priority seating area; use the elevators, never the escalators.
Bikes ride Metro SubwayLink outside rush hour and special events, at most two a car, in the priority seating area; use the elevators, never the escalators.
